question: UP-23 produced depth-stable scalar spectral moments, but they failed to decode the task. What is the highest-information next experiment?
evidence: Maximum spectral-moment drift at depth 1024 is near numerical zero, so invariance itself works.
Training and held-out task accuracy remain poor despite invariant features.
The transport has repeated eigenspaces inherited from the historical composite structure, so scalar moments can collapse orientation within multiplicity spaces.
constraints: Keep the recurrent 96-dimensional state fully mixed and block-free at runtime.
Do not restore visible semantic channel labels or runtime unmixing.
Test the multiplicity-space diagnosis directly before changing training budgets.

candidates.proposal: Increase the number of scalar spectral moments and training epochs without changing the observable algebra.
Use a sufficiently rich algebra of observables that commutes with the transport and can resolve orientation inside repeated eigenspaces while leaving the state fully mixed.
Undo the full-latent mixer at runtime and restore the six historical channel blocks.
Add held-out depths to training and tune ridge regularization until accuracy improves.

expected_why: A transport-commuting observable algebra directly tests whether lost multiplicity-space orientation caused the scalar-moment failure.
